title: TrustBound: A Mechanized Note on Payment-Epoch Completeness
abstract: Payment operations requested by an AI agent may remain executable, or their outcomes unresolved, after the agent has stopped. This paper studies the conditions under which a trusted payment service can account for all operations within a defined epoch and establish that no previously granted authority can produce further payments. We formalize an admission model in Lean in which each operation is recorded before execution authority is granted, and both actions are serialized with an admission fence. We prove that fencing fixes a journal covering all modeled effects and outstanding rights. Once those rights are discharged, the effect history remains unchanged; truthful outcomes for the recorded identities then establish exact identity-level accounting. A complementary provider-contract model requires registration before activation and keeps unregistered objects inert. The artifact checks 14 formal results and rejects eight premise-removal mutations. Implementation evidence comprises six service histories with 66 transitions checked in Lean, together with 864 bounded execution schedules checked in Python. The contribution is a payment-specific formalization of established closure principles, supported by explicit trust assumptions and reproducible implementation checks. The results are conditional on the stated contracts and do not establish correctness for all implementation executions or real payment providers.
